What's included

  • 4 × nights at Sigló Hotel (4-star, ocean-front)
  • 4 × 3-course dinners at Sigló Restaurant
  • 4 × daily breakfast buffet at Sigló Hotel
  • 4 × lunches at the Club House K2 Ski
  • Full ski equipment — skis, boots, poles
  • Ski shuttle to the clubhouse, 5 minutes away
  • Outdoor hot tub & sauna — unlimited access
  • Daily yoga & morning stretches

Where the helicopter ends, the adventure begins.

The Troll Peninsula is one of the last great untouched ski frontiers on earth — a vast, largely unexplored Arctic wilderness in Northern Iceland where the mountains rise straight out of the sea. Here, you ski from peaks all the way down to the shoreline of the North Atlantic, with no lift lines, no crowds, and often no tracks but your own.

Heli-Assisted Touring is the best of both worlds. A helicopter does the heavy lifting, then you earn your turns the way ski-touring lovers cherish — skinning up between towering peaks, into silent valleys few people ever reach. New to touring? This is the perfect way in, guided every step by IFMGA-certified mountain guides who have skied this peninsula their whole lives.

Ski beneath the midnight sun in spring, or chase the Northern Lights in early season. Powder, spring corn, untouched lines — and at night, a hot tub, a sauna, and a 4-star ocean-front room waiting in the fishing village of Siglufjörður.

A typical day, run by run

The helicopter lifts you to the first summit, and you carve your opening descent through untouched snow. At the bottom, you fit your skins and climb back up alongside your guide — then ski down for your second run. As you finish, the helicopter is already waiting to lift you to fresh terrain. You ski your third descent, switch back to skins, and earn your way to the top once more. Your fourth and final run of the day brings you down to the valley, where the helicopter collects you and flies you home to the clubhouse — and a well-earned meal and après-ski.

Four big descents every day. Two helicopter lifts, two skinned ascents — and you continue like this for four days in a row.

Typical heliskiing day*

  1. 07:00–09:00Enjoy a hearty breakfast at the hotel to fuel up for the day.
  2. 08:30–09:00Pick-up for a quick 3-minute drive to the Clubhouse, where your skis or snowboard await you for a day of fun and excitement. Our guides will review the day's plan, ensuring you are well-prepared and informed.
  3. 09:45–10:00Helicopters are ready to take you on an exhilarating day of skiing.
  4. 12:30–13:30Get ready for lunch with a view! You will get the opportunity to enjoy your meal with stunning views and great company.
  5. 15:00–16:00Return to the Clubhouse, where après ski awaits. Delicious, freshly prepared food and a variety of drinks to refresh your body and mind. Here you have the chance to talk about the day and exchange stories, photos, and videos with upbeat music in the background. You can also head back to the hotel for a dip in the hot tub, explore the town, try kayaking, visit the local brewery, or join some of the other activities we offer before it's time for dinner.
  6. 20:00A three-course dinner will be served at the hotel. Throughout your stay, you will get a variety of dishes locally sourced from Icelandic nature, such as cod, salmon, lamb, and more. After dinner is the perfect time for drinks around the fireplace.

*This is a sample itinerary as times and schedule may vary depending on weather conditions

Questions

Heli-assisted touring,answered.

How much does heli-assisted ski touring in Iceland cost?

From €3,490 for 3 days, €4,690 for 4 days and €5,590 for 5 days, twin per guest, full board at the 4-star Sigló Hótel — the most affordable way to ski the Troll Peninsula. Booking through us costs the same as booking direct.

What is heli-assisted ski touring?

The best of both worlds: the helicopter does the heavy lifting with two heli runs a day, then you earn your turns with a skinned ascent into quiet valleys. It is a superb introduction to touring, guided throughout by IFMGA guides.

How is it different from classic heliskiing?

Classic heliskiing is pure helicopter access with no climbing. Heli-assisted touring mixes heli lifts with skinning — fewer flights, a lower price, more backcountry feel. Expect about four big descents a day.

Do I need touring experience?

No — it is designed as the perfect way into touring, with your IFMGA guide teaching the skills as you go. A reasonable level of fitness and confident off-piste skiing help you enjoy it most.

What is included?

Nights at the 4-star Sigló Hótel, full board, ski or splitboard touring equipment, a BCA avalanche safety kit, IFMGA guiding, and unlimited hot tubs and sauna. Flights and travel insurance are not included.

How many runs and ascents will I do?

A typical day is two helicopter runs and one skinned ascent — about four big descents — repeated each day, for 12, 16 or 20 ascents across a 3, 4 or 5-day trip.

Does booking through Heliski Travel cost extra?

No — we are the authorised agent, so it costs exactly the same as booking direct, plus honest advice on whether touring or classic suits you. Ask us anything.
